solarPowerW.note: 788 W maximum from three body panels, per the company FCC filing (opened source). A secondary web page says 200 W [S*]; the two conflict, and we follow the rule that the opened source wins (same rule as the battery: 1,554 Wh over 700 Wh). The solar figure does not feed any verdict.

batteryWh.note: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Orbital Debris Assessment Report (FCC filing), page 9 of 52: three 72-cell Li-ion modules, 28 VDC nominal, total energy capacity per spacecraft 1554 W-h. A second FCC document (fcc.report SAT-LOA-20210423-00055) gives the same number. A secondary web page says 700 Wh; the two conflict. This is a pre-launch document, so the flown design may differ. Applies to the Nova-C design flown as IM-1 and IM-2; IM-2 may differ slightly.

heaterW.note: Team assumption for the whole night load (heater plus electronics), not the heater alone. Basis: Intuitive Machines said IM-1 had roughly 10 to 20 hours of battery left after sunset (Reuters, Feb 2024). With 1554 Wh that implies about 78 to 155 W; we take 100 W, about the middle of the hours range (15 h gives about 104 W). Not a published figure.
